farms.name: Super Smelter (furnace array)
farms.principle: Items and fuel are split across many furnaces by hoppers so smelting throughput scales with furnace count; outputs merge back into one chest.
caveats: Use blast furnaces for ores/metals (2x speed) and regular furnaces for food/logs; balance fuel distribution.

farms.name: Item Sorting System
farms.principle: Hopper lines with comparator-read filter hoppers (item + 4 stacked filler items) divert each item type into its own storage, auto-sorting a whole farm network.
farms.rate: throughput = hopper speed (2.5 items/s per lane)
caveats: Each filter needs the target item + 4 non-stackable/other items to bias the comparator; add overflow handling for full chests.

farms.name: Bulk Storage System (with sorter + overflow)
farms.principle: A wall of double chests/barrels fed by an item sorter, with an overflow loop back to the input and a signal-strength full indicator, forms a scalable warehouse.
caveats: Design overflow so a full category doesn't back up the whole hopper line; comparators can drive a 'full' lamp.

farms.name: Villager Trading Hall (mending librarians)
farms.principle: Isolated villagers are assigned lecterns and re-rolled until they offer wanted trades (Mending, Silk Touch, etc.); cheap emerald trades and enchanted books flow from a stall array.
caveats: Trade prices scale with demand and were rebalanced in the 1.21 line; re-roll unemployed librarians by breaking/replacing the lectern until the desired book appears.

farms.name: Auto-Crafter Array (1.21 Crafter)
farms.principle: The Crafter block, pulsed by redstone and fed by hoppers, auto-crafts recipes (rails, sticks, paper, dyes, food) turning raw farm output into finished items.
caveats: Crafter (added 1.21) enables fully-automatic crafting; use a comparator on the crafter to only fire when the grid is full.

farms.name: Block Compactor (ingots -> blocks)
farms.principle: A Crafter fed 9-at-a-time compresses ingots/nuggets/resources into blocks (iron/gold/copper/etc.) to save storage space and simplify transport.
caveats: Only fires when 9 items fill the grid (comparator on crafter); great tail-end for iron/gold farms.

farms.name: Automatic Brewing Station
farms.principle: Hoppers and droppers feed brewing stands in sequence (water bottles, nether wart, then the effect ingredient and gunpowder/redstone), auto-producing stacks of potions.
caveats: Sequence matters: nether wart first (awkward potion), then the effect ingredient, then modifiers (redstone/glowstone/gunpowder). Blaze powder fuels the stand.

farms.name: Wandering Trader Farm/Trap
farms.principle: Wandering traders that spawn near the player are trapped and killed for leads (and their llamas), a renewable source of leads and rare plants via trades.
caveats: Killing a leashed trader llama or trader drops leads; spawn rate is slow and tied to the wandering trader spawn cycle.

farms.name: Mob Switch (cap filler)
farms.principle: A large group of persistent mobs is kept loaded far away to fill a spawn category's mob cap, stopping natural spawns elsewhere so targeted farms (or perimeters) run at full rate.
farms.y_level: loaded but out of the way
caveats: Technical control device; only affects the chosen cap category. Some servers restrict chunk-loaders. Name-tag or otherwise persist the mobs.

farms.name: Nether Portal Item Transport
farms.principle: Items dropped through a linked nether portal traverse the 8:1 distance instantly in the other dimension; a hopper/dropper stream ships farm output across huge distances cheaply.
caveats: Portal linking must be precise so items arrive at the intended receiver; a collection water stream + hoppers catch items on the far side.

farms.name: TNT/Flying-Machine Tunnel Bore
farms.principle: A flying machine pushes TNT/instant-mine heads through stone, clearing large tunnels or perimeters; drops are swept up for bulk stone/ore and cleared spawn perimeters.
caveats: TNT-based bores rely on TNT duplication; disabled on many servers. Used to dig perimeters for high-rate mob/gold farms.

farms.name: Auto Shulker Box Loader/Unloader
farms.principle: Hoppers fill shulker boxes to a set count (comparator) then a piston/dispenser cycles a fresh box; a matching unloader empties boxes back into storage — bulk transport packaging.
caveats: Pairs with a shulker farm for endless boxes; comparator detects a full box before ejecting it.

farms.name: Auto Food Smoker (cooked food)
farms.principle: Smokers cook raw meat/food at double speed; hoppers feed raw food from animal farms and pull cooked food to storage, closing the food loop automatically.
caveats: Smokers only cook food items (2x speed); use dried kelp blocks or charcoal as renewable fuel.

farms.name: Zombie Villager Curing Station (cheap trades)
farms.principle: Zombie villagers are cured with a splash Potion of Weakness + golden apple; a cured villager gives massive permanent trade discounts, making enchanted books/gear cheap.
caveats: Discount from repeated curing was capped/rebalanced in recent versions, but a single cure still gives strong permanent discounts. Keep the villager near the cure spot (gossip range).
